summary: In space operations, a spent SpaceX rocket stage slammed into the moon, prompting NASA and astronomers to attempt observations of the lunar impact site. Meanwhile, NASA achieved a key hardware milestone by mating the Orion Crew and Service Modules for the Artemis III mission, as the Perseverance rover on Mars captured images of Earth vanishing behind the moon Phobos. In space science, preliminary test results from NASA’s PUNCH mission demonstrated improved solar storm forecasting capabilities, while observations from the IXPE observatory may have validated a 90-year-old astrophysical theory. On the defense front, Canada awarded Telesat a $1.63 billion contract for Arctic military satellite communications, and the U.S. Space Force awarded $615 million in contracts across three firms—including Rocket Lab—for airborne-target tracking technology. Concurrently, the National Reconnaissance Office issued new synthetic aperture radar data contracts to Capella Space, Iceye, and Umbra. In commercial developments, Blue Origin linked a recent New Glenn explosion to a rocket engine valve, SpaceX reported its second-quarter earnings alongside plans for an upcoming orbital Starship test, and European space situational awareness firm Neuraspace raised $18 million in new funding. Looking ahead, observers and researchers are preparing for an August 12 total solar eclipse that will darken skies across Greenland, Iceland, and Spain.
